name: Electronic Frontier Foundation
body: A content security policy in report-only mode, nosniff, framing limited to its origin, and a sitemap. But no page analyzed sends Strict-Transport-Security, so browsers don't upgrade a first http visit.
lesson: Add Strict-Transport-Security with a long max-age. It tells browsers to use https before the request leaves.
summary: www.eff.org scores 83 out of 100 (B). 1 check fails now, 19 are at risk, and 17 pass. Fix first: HSTS is not sent.

fix.title: HSTS is not sent
fix.evidence: strict-transport-security was absent on the start page. Missing on all 20 pages analyzed. A first visit over http can be intercepted.

fix.title: No content security policy
fix.evidence: content-security-policy was absent on the start page. Missing on all 20 pages analyzed. Injected scripts are not limited by the browser.
fix.fix: Start with the Report-Only policy in the fix kit, watch the reports for a week, then enforce it.

fix.title: 20 images have no alt attribute
fix.fix: Describe informative images. Give decorative ones alt="".

fix.title: 8 pages have no meta description
fix.evidence: /, /about/staff, /work, /updates and 4 more. Google and AI answers then write their own snippet from whatever text they find.
fix.fix: Write a 50 to 160 character description for each page that says what a reader gets.

fix.title: Referrer-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Browsers fall back to their default. An explicit policy keeps full URLs from leaking to other sites. Missing on all 20 pages analyzed.

fix.title: Permissions-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Embedded content can ask for the camera, microphone, or location. Missing on all 20 pages analyzed.

works.title: Every internal link that was opened answered
AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page
Plain http redirects permanently to https
The start page declares its language
The start page arrived in 227 ms
Share cards have a title, description, image, and URL
